Reading about it as we speak. Thanks for the tip.

Assuming you are referring to the WAN IP (this is the ip address used to reach your router from outside your home), no.

WAN IPs are assigned to providers in blocks and you will either pull a random IP (dhcp) or you will always be assigned the same IP (static) in either case that IP will always be from the providers assigned block.

You can get a VPN which will allow you to chose an egress point in another country but that egress point's IP will be assigned to the VPN provider.

It sounds like your best bet is to get a VPN and configure the router to connect directly to your account. (Don't forget to also resolve all DNS requests to the VPN provider rather than your ISP).

P.S. regarding:

the router in order for all devices within the network that connect to it, to get IP addresses in a different country.

All your local devices run on their own subnet which is only visible from within your network (LAN) Only the WAN IP assigned to your modem is visible the the outside world, all LAN traffic is translated at the router.

I do this with a pfSense firewall on a generic dual nic appliance. I use something similar to this Protectli Vault 2 Port, Firewall Micro Appliance with pfSense loaded on it. The WAN side of the firewall connects to the router and routes all traffic through a virtual WAN in a VPN tunnel. All DNS traffic is handled through the VPN as well. Certainly not foolproof but it works for me.
